title: Telemetry Incident Simulation Lab and Canonical Fixes
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This page describes a repeatable, low-risk telemetry incident simulation lab targeted at the Developer Experience (DevX) org. The lab is intended to: exercise SDK and docs-site telemetry pipelines, validate alerting and runbooks, produce canonical fixes for common failure modes, and create reproducible artifacts for support engineers and SDK owners.

Goals

- Verify end-to-end telemetry from client SDKs through our ingestion pipeline to the docs-site and alerting hooks.
- Validate common incident triage flows and reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) by producing canonical fixes.
- Provide a safe environment for engineers and on-call to practise runbook steps without impacting production.
- Produce a set of quickstart templates and API examples that include telemetry hooks and debug helpers.

Scope and Non-Goals

- In scope: SDK telemetry (Python/Node), ingestion (collector), processing (transform), storage, alerting notifications (PagerDuty/Slack), and docs-site debug pages.
- Out of scope: production traffic, customer PII, and long-term retention changes.

Ownership and Contacts

- Lab owner: Ava Martinez (devx-observability)
- SRE contact: Marco Ruiz (eng-sre)
- SDK owner: Priya Desai (sdk-team)
- Support liaison: Liam O'Connor (customer-success)
- PagerDuty: #redwood-devx-observability oncall (rotation policy in eng-sre/runbooks)

Prerequisites and Environment

1) Sandbox cluster: use the DevX sandbox cluster (k8s-devx-sandbox).
2) Test tenants: create two test tenants (tenant-alpha, tenant-beta) using the standard sandbox provisioning script.
3) Credentials: ephemeral API keys provisioned via CLI: redwoodctl iam create-key --ttl 4h --scope sandbox.
4) Tooling: kubectl v1.28, redwoodctl v0.12+, jq, curl, Python 3.10, Node 18.

Quick start: Provisioning

1. Create tenants:
   - redwoodctl tenant create tenant-alpha --env sandbox
   - redwoodctl tenant create tenant-beta --env sandbox
2. Create keys and export env var:
   - export RW_API_KEY=$(redwoodctl iam create-key --tenant tenant-alpha --ttl 4h --json | jq -r '.key')
3. Deploy the telemetry shim to the sandbox cluster:
   - kubectl apply -f https://internal.redwood.dev/observability/telemetry-shim/sandbox-deploy.yaml

Lab scenarios (high level)

Each scenario below contains: objective, simulation steps, expected signals, and canonical fixes. Run scenarios sequentially or in parallel as testers prefer.

Scenario A — SDK dropped-span / missing traces

Objective: Simulate missing distributed traces for a high-frequency SDK client and validate alerting and root cause.

Simulation steps:
1) Use the python demo app included in /examples/telemetry to generate traffic: python examples/telemetry/emit_spans.py --rate 500 --tenant tenant-alpha
2) Inject a client-side bug: set environment variable RW_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING=0 to force sampler to drop spans.
3) Observe ingestion: query the sampler metrics endpoint on telemetry-collector: curl http://telemetry-collector.devx.svc/metrics | grep sampling_drop_count

Expected signals:
- Spike in request count (ingress), but trace coverage drops to < 5%.
- Alert: trace-coverage < 10% for 5m triggers P1 in devx-observability.
- Docs site debug page shows large gap in span-correlator graph for tenant-alpha.

Canonical fixes:
- Roll client config back: set RW_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING=auto and restart client.
- If sampling config not found in runtime, update SDK default config to fallback to "auto" and add a warning to logs: "telemetry: sampling unset, using auto".
- Create a quickstart snippet for Python and Node that sets explicit sampling and emits a diagnostic span on startup.

Scenario B — Ingestion pipeline backpressure (collector memory pressure)

Objective: Reproduce transient ingestion backpressure when the collector is overwhelmed, and validate autoscaling and retry behavior.

Simulation steps:
1) Start a high-throughput generator using Node: node examples/telemetry/high_throughput.js --qps 2000 --tenant tenant-beta
2) On the collector deployment, temporarily set resource request to a low value: kubectl patch deploy telemetry-collector -n devx --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory","value":"200Mi"}]'
3) Watch for retry and queue metrics: curl http://telemetry-collector.devx.svc/metrics | grep requeue_count

Expected signals:
- Metric: collector_queue_length spikes above 500 for >2m.
- Alert: collector-queue-length > 300 for 2m -> page oncall.
- SDK clients see increased latency for telemetry ack endpoints; application-level generation continues.

Canonical fixes:
- Revert resource patch and scale collector to recommended profile: kubectl scale deploy telemetry-collector --replicas 3 -n devx.
- Update autoscaler policy: use queue length >200 as scale-up trigger and cooldown 30s.
- Add SDK client-side backoff: integrate standard retry with jitter and exponential cap (see code sample below).

Scenario C — Corrupted payload (invalid JSON)

Objective: Validate that the transform layer rejects corrupted payloads gracefully and surfaces structured error metrics for support.

Simulation steps:
1) Send a malformed payload: curl -X POST http://ingest.devx.svc/events -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_API_KEY" -d '{"spans": [ { "id": "abc", "payload": "\u0000\u0000" } ] }'
2) Observe transform errors: curl http://transform.devx.svc/metrics | grep parse_error_count

Expected signals:
- parse_error_count increments.
- A low-latency alert: transform-parse-errors > 10 in 1m -> create support ticket.
- The processing pipeline emits an event to the debug topic with payload id and raw bytes for forensic analysis.

Canonical fixes:
- Implement defensive parsing: return 422 + JSON body describing error with sample bytes and recommended remediation.
- Enhance SDKs to validate payloads client-side and redact problematic characters before send.

Triage runbook (step-by-step)

1) Initial assess (0-5m):
   - Check primary dashboards: trace-coverage, collector-queue-length, transform-parse-errors.
   - Identify affected tenants via metrics tagging.
2) Contain (5-15m):
   - For client-only issues: disable offending SDK release via feature flag or revoke ephemeral key for the test tenant.
   - For collector/backpressure: scale collector replicas and increase resources.
3) Investigate (15-60m):
   - Pull logs: kubectl logs -l app=telemetry-collector -n devx --since=1h | grep ERROR
   - Retrieve problematic payloads from debug topic: redwoodctl pubsub read debug-telemetry --limit 100 --filter tenant=tenant-alpha
4) Resolve (60m+):
   - Apply canonical fixes (see mapping table below).
   - Run verification: replay repaired payloads using examples/telemetry/replay.py.

Canonical fix mapping

| Scenario | Root cause (most common) | First-line fix | Follow-up change | Owner |
|--------|--------------------------|----------------|------------------|-------|
| Missing traces | Sampling misconfiguration in SDK | Reset RW_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING to auto | SDK: default to auto, add startup diagnostic span | sdk-team |
| Collector backpressure | Insufficient replicas/resources | Scale telemetry-collector to 3+ replicas | Autoscaler policy update | eng-sre |
| Corrupted payload | Client JSON encoding bug | Reject with 422 + debug event | SDK client-side validation & escape helpers | devx-observability |

Debugging tools and quick snippets

Python: emit diagnostic span on startup

```python
from redwood_sdk import Telemetry
telemetry = Telemetry(api_key=os.environ['RW_API_KEY'])
telemetry.emit({"name": "startup.diagnostic", "tags": {"version": "0.1"}})
```

Node: exponential retry template

```js
async function sendWithRetry(sendFn, attempts=5) {
  for (let i = 0; i < attempts; i++) {
    try {
      return await sendFn();
    } catch (err) {
      const backoff = Math.min(1000 * Math.pow(2, i) + Math.random() * 100, 5000);
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, backoff));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('exhausted retries');
}
```

Observable checks and SLOs used in lab

- Trace coverage SLO: >= 75% measured per tenant over 5m windows. Alert when <10% for 5m.
- Collector queue length SLO: median < 50, alert if >300 for 2m.
- Transform parse error SLO: 0 per 10m; page if >10 in 1m.

Post-simulation artifacts and docs updates

After each lab run do the following:
1) Capture dashboards as PNGs and attach to the incident ticket.
2) Update the SDK quickstart templates to include the diagnostic span snippet and explicit sampling example.
3) Publish a short support note in the support-top-issues space summarizing the reproduce steps and canonical fixes. Use the following checklist:
   - Repro steps written and verified (Y/N)
   - Fatal metrics and alerts validated (Y/N)
   - Quickstart snippets added to repo (Y/N)
   - Postmortem template pre-filled for internal run (Y/N)

Docs site operating procedures (for maintainers)

- Location for snippets: docs-repo/devx/snippets/telemetry/
- Merge policy: all changes must include a verified sandbox replay and a snippet test that runs in CI (snippets are executed in a snippet-runner container).
- Release cadence: publish doc changes after two successful sandbox runs. Major behavior changes require a canary publish and a support playbook update.

Support and escalation guidance

- Use the devx-observability PagerDuty rotation for P1 pages.
- For incidents that affect multiple tenants, trigger an incident commander and notify customer-success lead for affected test tenants.
- If a canonical fix requires an SDK change, open a standard SDK RFC and tag it "telemetry-hotfix" for expedited review.

Appendix: Useful CLI commands and endpoints

- redwoodctl tenant list --env sandbox
- redwoodctl iam create-key --tenant tenant-alpha --ttl 4h --json
- kubectl get pods -n devx -l app=telemetry-collector
- curl http://telemetry-collector.devx.svc/metrics | grep queue_length
- redwoodctl pubsub read debug-telemetry --limit 100 --filter tenant=tenant-alpha
